prompt: Use showntell to make me a narrated walkthrough of src/showntell/format.py: how the incremental Markdown parser works and why chunk boundaries matter.
Use showntell to make a narrated walkthrough of what changed between commits 8d0619a and f2a4a93 in this repo, for a reviewer.
Use showntell to give me an architecture overview of this project: the daemon, the MCP tools, speech, and the player. Keep it under three minutes.
Use showntell to explain how word timings from the speech model become pointer cues in this project. Look at src/showntell/speech/narrator.py and src/showntell/static/js/timeline.js.
Use showntell to explain how DNS resolution works, from typing a URL to getting an IP address.
Use showntell to explain how a hash map handles collisions, with a short code example.
Use showntell to explain gradient descent: the update rule, the learning rate, and a tiny worked example.
Use showntell to explain the TCP three-way handshake and why it needs three steps.
Use showntell to explain how CSRF attacks work and how SameSite cookies prevent them.
Use showntell to explain git rebase versus merge, with diagrams of the commit graph.
Use showntell to show how the parse_tree function in src/showntell/kinds/tree.py could be made simpler, walking through the code as it changes step by step.
Use showntell to show how one add_slides call travels from the coding agent through the stdio shim, the daemon, the builder and the narrator, and into the browser player.

Use showntell to explain how MP4 export got faster: the first version rendered at 3.6 times real time, skipping unchanged frames reached 8.3, a faster x264 preset 10.2, and JPEG frames 16. Show the numbers and what each change did.

Use showntell to show a new contributor how to set up this repo and run its tests: the commands from the README and CONTRIBUTING, real output from `uv run pytest --collect-only -q` and `uv run showntell --help` (you may run those two), and where the tests live.
Use showntell to explain what an MCP client and server say to each other when a tool is called: initialize, tools/list and tools/call, with the messages they exchange.
Use showntell to explain why the sky is blue.
Use showntell to explain what causes ocean tides, and why most coasts get two a day.
Use showntell to explain why Earth has seasons.
Use showntell to explain how a magnifying glass focuses light.
